<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Business and economy'''
*[[News Media Bargaining Code]]
**[[Facebook]] bans [[Australia]]n news publishers from posting and Australian users from viewing or sharing any news content in a preemptive retaliation against the [[Australian Competition & Consumer Commission]]'s proposed News Media Bargaining Code, which would require it to pay to host Australian news content. A number of key government and charity organisations were also blocked for several hours. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2021/feb/18/facebook-blocks-health-departments-charities-and-its-own-pages-in-botched-australia-news-ban (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Alphabet Inc.]] agrees to begin paying [[News Corp]] for news content. News Corp [[CEO]] [[Robert Thomson (executive)|Robert Thomson]] credits the ACCC's proposed legislation with making the deal possible. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/17/technology/facebook-google-australia-news.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 lockdowns|Lockdown restrictions]] are eased in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] as contact tracers are confident all cases linked to a recent outbreak are [[self-isolating]]. People are permitted to leave their homes for any reason, but required to wear a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask]] indoors. Private gatherings of up to 5 people and public gatherings of up to 20 are permitted once again. Non-essential businesses and on-campus learning are reopened, and businesses that were working from home can return up to 50% of their workforce to the office. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/feb/17/victorias-lockdown-to-lift-at-midnight-but-some-restrictions-remain-in-place (''The Guardian'')]
****[[South Australia]] reopens its land border with Victoria to the state's regional population, while still restricting travellers from [[Melbourne]], the location of the recent outbreak. Similar restrictions remain at the [[New South Wales]] and [[Tasmania]] borders. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-update-border-restrictions-lifted-with-regional-victoria/6c6a67d3-2e3c-406f-964c-e4e51c9a0ec3 (9 News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****Restrictions ease in [[New Zealand]], with [[Auckland]] downgrading to alert level 2 and the rest of the country to alert level 1. Most Auckland schools are reopened and masks are made mandatory on public transport. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/covid-19-coronavirus-auckland-to-level-2-rest-of-nz-to-level-1-despite-another-new-covid-case/N6OMWI6DLL4NLJGZ6AN7I2AHTU/ (''New Zealand Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] grants [[emergency use authorization]] to [[Sinovac]]'s [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], making it the city's second vaccine to be approved. [https://qz.com/1974171/hong-kong-just-approved-chinas-sinovac-covid-19-vaccine/amp/ (Quartz)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 25 new deaths in the past 24 hours and surpasses 1,000 deaths of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/02/18/covid-19-2712-new-cases-highest-daily-deaths-of-25-bring-total-fatalities-to-1030 (''The Star'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] approves the emergency use of [[Sinopharm]]'s [[vaccine]], which become the second vaccine to be approved in the country. [https://www.deccanherald.com/international/world-news-politics/nepal-approves-chinas-sinopharm-covid-19-vaccine-to-purchase-astrazeneca-shots-from-india-952564.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]]'s Food and Drug Authority approves the use of [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/saudi/covid-19-saudi-arabia-approves-oxford-astrazeneca-vaccine-1.77287875 (''Gulf News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****[[Nigeria]] approves the emergency use of [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] produced by the [[Serum Institute of India]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/amp/news/articles/2021-02-18/nigeria-approves-astrazeneca-vaccines-for-emergency-use (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] begins its vaccination programme against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] starting with [[health workers]] using China's [[Sinopharm]] vaccine. Health minister and [[Vice President of Zimbabwe|vice president]] [[Constantino Chiwenga]] is the first person to receive the vaccine. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/zimbabwe-begins-covid-19-vaccination-with-chinese-jabs/2149125 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nevada]]
****[[Nevada]] reports their first case of [[501.V2 variant]] in a person who travelled from [[South Africa]] and began showing symptoms of COVID-19 when arrived in [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/best-states/nevada/articles/2021-02-18/nevada-reports-1st-case-of-virus-variant-from-south-africa (''U.S. News and World Report'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
***Lab studies suggest the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] and [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]]s are significantly less effective in providing antibody protection against the [[501.V2 variant]] of the disease, most prevalent in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/feb/18/south-african-covid-variant-may-cut-pfizer-vaccine-protection-by-two-thirds (''The Guardian'')]

'''Science and Technology'''
*[[Mars 2020]]
**The rover [[Perseverance (rover)|''Perserverance'']] successfully lands on [[Mars]] as part of the [[Mars 2020]] mission. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2021/02/18/science/nasa-mars-landing (''The New York Times'')]
